title: upgrade attention kernels: flashattnv2 + fused ops + rope/rotary + kv-batching + scheduling
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops; improved KV-cache batching and scheduler heuristics. P99 latency reduced and throughput increased for large-context models. Backwards compatible with existing model artifacts; rollout will be canary then fleet-wide.
body:
Context and motivation:
We have multiple customer workloads showing latency spikes and suboptimal GPU utilization for long-context generative workloads. FlashAttentionV2 yields substantial compute efficiency improvements, and combining it with fused rotary/ROPE operations and targeted KV-cache batching reduces memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead. This PR implements a coordinated upgrade across kernels, KV reuse paths, and the request scheduler to capture those gains while preserving numerical compatibility and fallbacks for older CUDA toolchains.

What this PR changes (single-string description):
- Integrates FlashAttentionV2 kernels into the serving runtime with a feature flag (runtime.kernels.flashattn_v2).
- Adds fused rotary/ROPE fused-ops path to the attention forward/backward kernels where supported by the model config (rotary/rope autodetect).
- Reworks KV-cache handling to introduce continuous-batching-aware coalescing: we now aggregate small KV write workloads into larger batched updates when latency headroom is available.
- Updates the scheduler heuristics to prefer keeping affinity of long-context streams on the same worker to maximize KV cache hit-rate, and adds a new dynamic split policy when GPU memory pressure exceeds threshold.
- Adds compatibility layer to fall back to FlashAttentionV1 or non-fused kernels when GPU capability or toolchain version is incompatible.
- Adds unit and integration tests for fused op correctness, plus a new end-to-end perf job in CI comparing before/after p50/p95/p99 timings on representative LLM configs.

Implementation notes and tradeoffs:
- Kernel selection is now done at model load time and memoized per model-version/quantization combo. We probe for CUDA arch, driver, and cuBLAS/cuDNN/hip equivalents, and expose a runtime flag for operators to force old kernels for troubleshooting.
- Fused ROPE/rotary path reduces memory traffic by fusing the rotary multiplication into the attention Q/K projection kernel for supported dtypes. We keep a non-fused slow path that is functionally identical for numeric parity.
- KV coalescing adds a micro-queue in the worker which is drained on either size or time thresholds; the time threshold is conservative to avoid added tail latency.
- Scheduler changes prioritize locality; stress-tested on 2k concurrent synthetic streams with variable sequence lengths.

Benchmark summary (see benchmark_summary field for numbers):
All benchmarks run on n1-standard G5 instances with A100-equivalent testbed and representative 32k-context T5-style model. Representative wins after enabling feature flag and running 10-minute steady-state: p99 latency -18%, p50 latency -10%, throughput +22% for long-context workloads; memory traffic reduced by ~14%. Short-context workloads show negligible change.

Testing and CI:
- New unit tests and integration tests added.
- A perf CI job (ci/perf/attn-upgrade) added that runs a 10-minute steady-state comparison; results uploaded to perf-dashboard.
- Initial CI run failed due to an off-by-one in the rotary offset handling; fixed in second commit and rerun passed.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime.kernels.flashattn_v2 with default disabled for existing customers.
- Canary: enable for 5% of traffic for low-risk customers for 48h with automatic rollback on key regressions (p99 latency +15% or error-rate +0.5%).
- Incremental ramp to 100% with monitoring of KV-hit metrics, p99 latency, and OOM events.

Backward compatibility:
- Models compiled/quantized with older toolchains will continue to use legacy kernels; behavior is unchanged.
- No API surface changes.

Commits summary:
- "probe: detect flashattn_v2 support and expose runtime flag"
- "kernels: add flashattnv2 fused rotary/rope kernels"
- "kv-cache: introduce continuous-batch coalescing and micro-queue"
- "scheduler: locality-first affinity and dynamic split policy"
- "tests: add unit/integration and perf CI job"

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/kernels/flashattn_v2/* (new kernels and build hooks)
- runtime/scheduler/affinity_scheduler.py (heuristics and policy)
- runtime/kv_cache/coalescer.py (micro-queue implementation)
- runtime/model_loader/kernel_selector.py (selection/memoization logic)
- ci/perf/attn-upgrade.yml (perf job)
- tests/integration/test_fused_rotary.py (correctness tests)
- docs/ops/attn-kernels.md (docs + rollout notes)

Notes: the PR intentionally keeps the default off to reduce risk for older infra; the code includes detailed logging when fallbacks are used.

fix: off-by-one rotary offset in fused path (CI failure fix)
review_comments: Marcus Lee (reviewer): Can you add a guard to ensure the fused path is only enabled for FP16/BF16? Otherwise we risk precision regressions for FP32 models.
Asha Patel (author): Good catch — added dtype guards in kernel_selector and unit tests for FP32 fallbacks.

Riley Chen (reviewer): The scheduler change improves KV hit-rate in local testing, but we should ensure it doesn't create hotspotting on small clusters. Recommend adding a soft cap on affinity weight.
Asha Patel (author): Added soft cap and an optional randomized eviction to distribute streams when worker imbalance is detected.
Olivia Park (approver): Verified e2e perf job and unit tests. Approving pending CI green and a short canary plan in the release notes.
benchmark_summary: memory traffic: -14% (measured DRAM reads during attention)
